United States (Midwest / Washington D.C. / national fuel market)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation — YES *(references to first Trump term SRE expansion)*
T2. Forward-looking immediate — YES *(EPA decision expected end of August 2026; RIN market already reacting)*
T3. Long-term development — NO *(no structural, multi-year policy trajectory described)*

**Synopsis:**
The White House — driven by Stephen Miller, the Energy Dominance Council and fuel-price concerns linked to Strait of Hormuz disruption — is pressuring EPA to approve Small Refinery Exemptions (SREs) well above the projected ~1 billion RINs, potentially reaching 1.2–1.8 billion RINs, cutting into the record 26.81 billion RIN 2026 blending mandate. This pits the oil refining lobby against Farm Belt agricultural interests. RIN prices have already dropped to four-month lows. The backdrop is pump prices stubbornly above $4/gallon, with midterm elections creating political urgency.
